method: Receptor-model source attribution: non-negative matrix factorisation (the factor model behind EPA PMF; 6 factors, Kullback-Leibler loss) of 8 daily Copernicus CAMS tracers scaled by their 90th percentiles, over 11508 site-days at 84 reference sites (2024-09-27 to 2025-02-28). Factors are named by optimal (Hungarian) matching of their profiles to reference chemical signatures, and observed PM2.5 is apportioned by non-negative least squares on the factor activations plus an intercept (regional background & other).

factors.label: Traffic & urban combustion
factors.description: Freshly emitted nitric oxide (NO) with some NO2 from vehicle exhaust and other street-level combustion, strongest in calm winter air over big cities.

factors.label: Industry, coal & power
factors.description: Sulphur dioxide rising together with carbon monoxide and nitrogen dioxide, the signature of coal, power plants and industry; in this model it also carries much of a city's other fuel burning.

factors.label: Fires & biomass burning
factors.description: Formaldehyde-rich air from crop, forest and savanna fires and household biomass burning, although formaldehyde also forms from plant and urban emissions in hot or stagnant air.

factors.label: Desert dust
factors.description: Mineral dust blown from deserts and dry land such as the Sahara, Arabia and the Thar, often carried hundreds of kilometres.

factors.label: Photochemical & secondary
factors.description: Ozone-rich, chemically aged air in which sunlight turns gases into secondary particles; this regional haze is the baseline of PM2.5 almost everywhere.

factors.label: Sea salt (marine)
factors.description: Sea-salt spray from breaking ocean waves, carried inland by onshore winds at coastal sites.

checks.name: Traffic factor is higher on working days
checks.detail: Median over 80 sites of mean weekday / mean weekend traffic activation (local weekends: Fri-Sat in the Gulf states, Iraq, Egypt, Algeria and Bangladesh, Sat in Nepal, Sat-Sun elsewhere); 35/80 sites above 1. The raw CAMS NO2 input has a median ratio of 0.990 on the same days, i.e. the global model itself shows almost no weekly cycle.

checks.name: Sea-salt share is higher at coastal than inland sites
checks.detail: Mean marine share at 24 clearly coastal sites 0.000 vs 37 clearly inland sites 0.000. The marine factor activation itself is 0.950 at the coast vs 0.019 inland; its PM2.5 coefficient is 0.00 ug/m3 per unit activation.

checks.name: Desert-dust share is highest in the Middle East, North Africa and Sahel
checks.detail: Mean dust share by region (Sahel = N'Djamena, Dakar): Middle East & North Africa + Sahel 0.157, Sub-Saharan Africa 0.041, Central Asia & Caucasus 0.015, Latin America & Caribbean 0.014, South Asia 0.007, East Asia 0.004, Europe 0.003, North America 0.002, Southeast Asia 0.000. Top sites: Jeddah 0.357, N'Djamena 0.346, Kuwait City 0.317, Abuja 0.230, Doha 0.186.

checks.name: Burning factor peaks in the Oct-Nov crop-residue season (Delhi, Lahore)
checks.detail: Mean burning activation Oct-Nov 2024 / Dec 2024-Feb 2025: New Delhi 1.32, Lahore 0.79 (value = the lower ratio).

checks.name: Factor activations explain observed PM2.5
checks.detail: In-sample R2 of the NNLS regression of observed daily PM2.5 on the 6 activations + intercept over 11508 site-days at 84 monitors; out-of-fold R2 with location-grouped 5-fold CV 0.130; raw CAMS PM2.5 alone reaches R2 0.438 on the same rows.
